title: Book One · Chapter 65: The Arrow That Points Back
story:
Ronan spreads the map on the floor.

Leo lies beside it on his stomach. Between them is a small tin of pencil ends. They have one long pencil too. Neither boy wants to use the short green one.

“It makes my fingers tired,” Leo says.

“Then draw a small shop.”

“I am drawing the big road.”

Mum steps over them with a basket of cloth.

“The big road is in my way.”

They move closer to the bed.

The envelope is safe with Mrs Gao now. The map is still hard to follow. Someone new to the street could take a wrong turn. Ronan asked Mum to follow it after lunch. He wants her to reach East Court without a question.

“You know the way already,” Leo says.

“She can pretend.”

“I cannot pretend to miss a hole in the road,” Mum says. “Draw that too.”

They add the hole beside the tea shop. Leo draws a cart. It looks larger than the shop itself.

“That will not always be there,” Ronan says.

“Then it can move on the paper.”

He rubs out the cart. A grey mark stays on the paper.

After lunch, Mum takes the map. The boys follow three steps behind her. She turns left at the first corner.

“No!” Ronan calls.

Mum stops. “Your arrow says left.”

“That is for the way back.”

“How do I know?”

Ronan runs up. He looks from the paper to the corner. He holds the map towards home. Now the arrow points the right way. Mum holds it towards the river. Now it points the wrong way.

Leo turns it round. Now the names are upside down.

A man with a basket asks them to make room. They stand against the wall and let him pass.

Ronan feels hot. They worked hard to find the right gate. Now his map takes Mum away from it.

“We need a start,” Leo says.

Ronan looks at him.

“Like a game. Everyone starts here.”

He points to the green gate near their home.

Mum gives him the pencil. On the map, he draws a small foot beside that gate. Under it he writes START HERE. Leo adds a line for the walk there. A dotted line shows the walk back.

Leo wants to rub out every old line. Ronan holds the paper flat.

“Only this one is wrong.”

They check the school and Mr Qiu's stall. Both are still in the right place. Leo puts the rubber down. There is already one thin hole in the paper. They need the map for the walk home too.

They try again.

This time Mum gets to the tea shop. She finds the gate with the three stones. The hole is in the right place on the map.

“Do not step in our hole,” Leo says.

“It is not your hole.”

“We found it.”

“And someone else must fill it.”

Ronan folds the map carefully. They will make a clean one later. First they walk home by the dotted way.

At the first corner, Mum stops and hands him the basket she brought.

“Your map helped me. Now help me buy some greens.”

The boys choose between two piles. Leo wants the biggest leaves. Ronan looks for the leaves with fewer holes.

Mum buys a small bunch from each.

“Two shoppers for one soup,” she says.

Ronan carries both bunches home. He checks the little foot on the map. Now he can see the start of the walk.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- arrow＝箭头
- upside down＝上下颠倒
- make room＝让出地方
- dotted line＝点线

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：pretend＝假装；rub out＝擦掉。

## 读句提示

**Now his map takes Mum away from it.**

现在／他的地图／让妈妈离那扇门更远。it指上一句的right gate。

## 理解问题

1. 地图的第一个箭头为什么会让Mum走错？
2. Leo提出了什么办法来改进地图？
